jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The EHS Coordinator is responsible for supporting environmental, health, safety, and regulatory compliance programs within a manufacturing environment. This role partners with operations, quality, and maintenance teams to promote workplace safety, environmental compliance, food safety initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts.
Key Responsibilities

Environmental & Regulatory Compliance

Ensure compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety regulations.
Manage permits, reporting requirements, audits, and inspections.
Oversee waste management, stormwater, wastewater, hazardous materials, and pollution prevention programs.
Maintain EHS documentation, SDS records, and compliance files.
Monitor regulatory changes and implement program updates.

Health & Safety

Develop and maintain safety programs, procedures, and training.
Conduct risk assessments, inspections, and incident investigations.
Coordinate emergency response planning and preparedness activities.
Promote a strong safety culture and ensure contractor compliance.

Training & Continuous Improvement

Deliver employee safety and compliance training.
Lead safety meetings and awareness initiatives.
Track EHS metrics and support corrective actions.
Participate in sustainability, waste reduction, and continuous improvement projects.

Qualifications

3+ years of EHS experience in a manufacturing environment.
Working knowledge of OSHA, EPA, and related regulatory requirements.
Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Experience with audits, inspections, incident investigations, and compliance reporting.
Bachelor's degree in EHS, Engineering, Environmental Science, or related field preferred.
Bilingual Spanish preferred.

jobs.title: Building & Environmental Health Surveyor - Full Time
jobs.location: West Wyalong, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
As the Building & Environmental Health Surveyor you will be responsible for assessing applications, undertaking certification and inspections, investigating compliance matters and providing professional advice to Council, industry and the community.

The role offers a broad scope of work across residential, commercial and industrial development. Providing the opportunity to apply your technical expertise while contributing to safe, compliant and well-planned development across the shire.

What We Are Looking For In You

A technically capable and solution focused professional with relevant qualifications in building surveying, certification, environmental health or a related discipline and the ability to maintain the accreditation.
Demonstrated sound knowledge of Building Code of Australia, planning, public health and environmental legislation. Together with the ability to confidently interpret and apply legislation and technical requirements.
Proven experience across development assessment, building certification and inspections with the ability to work across residential, commercial and industrial development.
A strong regulatory and problem-solving mindset with experience investigating complaints, resolving compliance matters and achieving fair and practical outcomes.
Sound professional judgement, communication and report writing skills are essential, along with the ability to manage competing priorities, navigate complex matters and deliver practical outcomes.

What We Have To Offer

As a valued member of our team, you’ll receive the following benefits:

A family-based culture with genuine and friendly people to work with
Competitive salary and opportunity for salary progression
5 weeks annual leave
Access to 6.5 weeks long service leave after 5 years of service
Flexible work arrangements
9 day fortnight roster
Learning and career development opportunities
Subsidised Corporate Uniforms
Allowance, overtime and call out penalties when required
Hourly rate from $60.09
Plus, a 12% Council Superannuation contribution.

How You Can Apply

Before applying, please review the POSITION DESCRIPTION.

Please address the questions on the application page on the website. When responding to the questions, please include detailed relevant examples of your skills and experience.

You'll have the opportunity to attach your cover letter and resume.

For more information regarding the Building and Environmental Health Surveyor position, please contact Erin Green on (02) 6972 2266.

CLOSING DATE: 30 SEPTEMBER 2026
